examples.title: Example 1: Loading Images of Basic Types
examples.description: This example demonstrates how to load images of basic types, such as PNG, GIF, SVG, and JPG, by passing in Resource resources.

examples.title: Example 2: Downloading and Displaying Static Online Images
examples.description:
The default timeout is 5 minutes for loading online images. When using an online image, you are advised to use alt to configure a placeholder image displayed during loading. You can use HTTP to send a network request, and then decode the returned data into a PixelMap object for the Image component. Note that a GIF image loaded into a PixelMap object will be displayed as a static image. For details about image development, see the Image Kit overview.
The ohos.permission.INTERNET permission is required for using online images. For details about how to apply for a permission, see Declaring Permissions.

examples.title: Example 3: Downloading and Displaying Online GIF Images
examples.description:
This example shows how to use the cacheDownload.download API to download online GIF images.
The ohos.permission.INTERNET permission is required for using online images. For details about how to apply for a permission, see Declaring Permissions.

examples.title: Example 4: Adding Events to an Image
examples.description: This example demonstrates how to add the onClick and onFinish events to an image.

examples.title: Example 5: Enabling the AI Image Analyzer
examples.description: This example shows how to enable the AI image analyzer using the enableAnalyzer API.

examples.title: Example 6: Stretching an Image Using slice
examples.description: This example demonstrates how to stretch an image in different directions using the slice option of the resizable attribute.

examples.title: Example 7: Stretching an Image Using lattice
examples.description: This example demonstrates how to stretch an image using the lattice option of the resizable attribute with a rectangular lattice object.

examples.title: Example 8: Playing a PixelMap Array Animation
examples.description: This example demonstrates how to play an animation using a PixelMap array through an AnimatedDrawableDescriptor object.

examples.title: Example 9: Setting a Color Filter for an Image
examples.description: This example shows how to set a color filter for an image using the colorFilter attribute.

examples.title: Example 10: Setting the Fill Effect for an Image
examples.description: This example shows how to use the objectFit attribute to specify how an image is resized to fit its container.

examples.title: Example 11: Switching Between Different Types of Images
examples.description: This example demonstrates the effect of displaying images with ResourceStr and ImageContent as types of data sources.

examples.title: Example 12: Securing Sensitive Information
examples.description: This example shows how to secure sensitive information on widgets using the privacySensitive attribute. The display requires widget framework support.

examples.title: Example 13: Setting the Scan Effect for an Image
examples.description: This example shows how to enable the scan effect for an image using linearGradient and animateTo().

examples.title: Example 14: Adding Transform Effects to an Image
examples.description:
This example demonstrates how to apply rotation and translation effects to an image using the imageMatrix and objectFit attributes.
The imageMatrix attribute is added since API version 15.

examples.title: Example 15: Setting the Image Decoding Size Using sourceSize
examples.description: This example uses the sourceSize API to customize the image decoding size.

examples.title: Example 16: Setting the Image Rendering Mode Using renderMode
examples.description: This example uses the renderMode API to set the image rendering mode to grayscale.

examples.title: Example 17: Setting the Image Repeat Pattern Using objectRepeat
examples.description: This example uses the objectRepeat API to repeat the image along the vertical axis.

examples.title: Example 18: Setting the Fill Color for an SVG Image
examples.description: This example shows how to set different fill colors for an SVG image using the fillColor attribute.
examples.code:
@Entry
@Component
struct Index {
  build() {
    Column() {
      Text('FillColor not set')
      // Replace $r('app.media.svgExample') with the image resource file you use.
      Image($r('app.media.svgExample'))
        .height(100)
        .width(100)
        .objectFit(ImageFit.Contain)
        .borderWidth(1)
      Text('fillColor set to ColorContent.ORIGIN')
      // Replace $r('app.media.svgExample') with the image resource file you use.
      Image($r('app.media.svgExample'))
        .height(100)
        .width(100)
        .objectFit(ImageFit.Contain)
        .borderWidth(1)
        .fillColor(ColorContent.ORIGIN)
      Text('fillColor set to Color.Blue')
      // Replace $r('app.media.svgExample') with the image resource file you use.
      Image($r('app.media.svgExample'))
        .height(100)
        .width(100)
        .objectFit(ImageFit.Contain)
        .borderWidth(1)
        .fillColor(Color.Blue)
      Text('fillColor set to undefined')
      // Replace $r('app.media.svgExample') with the image resource file you use.
      Image($r('app.media.svgExample'))
        .height(100)
        .width(100)
        .objectFit(ImageFit.Contain)
        .borderWidth(1)
        .fillColor(undefined)
    }
    .height('100%')
    .width('100%')
  }
}

examples.title: Example 19: Adjusting HDR Image Brightness
examples.description:
This example demonstrates how to adjust the HDR image brightness using the hdrBrightness attribute, changing the value from 0 to 1.
The hdrBrightness attribute is added since API version 19.

examples.title: Example 20: Setting Whether the Image Follows the System Language Direction
examples.description: This example shows how to use the matchTextDirection API to set whether the image should be mirrored when the device system language is set to Uyghur.

examples.title: Example 21: Setting Image Display Orientation
examples.description: This example shows how to configure different image display orientations using the orientation attribute.

examples.title: Example 22: Using EXIF Metadata for Image Display Orientation
examples.description: This example demonstrates how to use the getImageProperty API to obtain the EXIF metadata of an image, and then set the image display orientation through the orientation attribute based on the obtained EXIF metadata.

examples.title: Example 23: Dynamically Switching an SVG Image Between Fill Colors
examples.description: This example demonstrates how to dynamically switch an SVG Image between fill colors across different color spaces using ColorMetrics.

examples.title: Example 24: Displaying an Image Using an App Sandbox Path
examples.description: This example demonstrates how to display an image using the app sandbox path, where a preloaded image named cloud.png is placed in the haps/entry/files directory of the current app.

examples.title: Example 25: Displaying an Image Using a Relative Path
examples.description: This example demonstrates how to display an image using a relative path. First, create a common directory at the same level as the project's pages directory. Then, place a preloaded image named cloud1.png in the common directory and display it using the relative path.

examples.title: Example 26: Displaying an SVG Image Using supportSvg2
examples.description:
In this example, the supportSvg2 attribute is set to enable the enhanced SVG tag parsing feature.
The supportSvg2 attribute is added since API version 21.

examples.title: Example 27: Implementing Fade-in/Fade-out Transition Effects for Images Using ContentTransition
examples.description: This example demonstrates how to use the contentTransition attribute to implement the fade-in/fade-out effect for smooth image transitions when the image source is switched on a click. This attribute is supported since API version 21.

examples.title: Example 28: Setting Loading and Load-Failure Images Using alt
examples.description: This example demonstrates how to display specified images during image loading and when image loading fails by setting the alt attribute.

examples.title: Example 29 Listening to Online Image Loading Exceptions Using onError
examples.description:
This example demonstrates how to obtain detailed download information (ImageError) when an online image fails to load via the onError callback. When image loading fails, you can obtain detailed online image download information through the downloadInfo attribute in ImageError, including download resource information, network request information, and performance statistics. This helps quickly identify the cause of network exceptions or resource errors.
The downloadInfo attribute is added to ImageError since API version 23.

examples.title: Example 30 Setting Anti-aliasing for Pixel Map Image Edges
examples.description:
This example demonstrates how to enable the anti-aliasing feature for pixel map image edges by setting the antialiased API.
The antialiased API is added since API version 23.
